messages:
SRE-Bot: ALERT: gpu-node-17 runtime 'inference-prod-7' reported CUDA OOM while reported headroom ~1.3GB. Auto-eviction triggered, container restarted by kube. Investigating. (evt=oom, code=CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY)
Alex: seeing repeated 500s for a subset of requests? which models were on that node?
InfraBot: pinned labels: gpu-type=A100-40GB, pool=dedicated-inference, pods:
  - inference-prod-7 (runtime v2.11)
  - model: open-llama-13b-8k (quantized)
Maria: root cause candidate: large contiguous allocation request failed despite free memory due to fragmentation + reserved blocks pinned by KV cache. Logs attached.
Jordan: logs? any nvml or driver errors?
InfraBot: attaching relevant snippets:
```
[2026-03-15T09:11:22Z] runtime: allocate 3.5GB for key/value cache chunk -> CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY
[2026-03-15T09:11:22Z] nvml: free=1.31GB, reserved=2.45GB, fragmented_small_blocks=1.9GB
[2026-03-15T09:11:22Z] allocator: contiguous_request=3.5GB failed, fallback to paged allocation -> OOM
```
Alex: so headroom (free) looked ok but fragmentation + reserved blocks prevented large contiguous alloc. That matches theory.
Sam: also noticed prefetch queue spikes just before OOM, kube container logs show prefetching next tokens. Possible microburst.
Maria: yep, prefetch was enabled for that runtime (PREFETCH_ENABLED=true). For these models prefetch tries to reserve contiguous slab then writes, which fails if slab fragmented.
Jordan: customers: any 5xx errors surfaced to clients? CS Lead: customer telemetry shows ~170 requests failed with 500 over 9m window; three tenants reported degraded latencies but retries mitigated for most. No SLA breach yet but close.
Alex: immediate mitigation options?
Maria: recommended hot fixes we can roll now:
  1) Temporarily disable prefetch on impacted runtime: set `PREFETCH_ENABLED=false` and restart runtime container (fast).
  2) Reduce kv_cache_reserve from 2.5GB -> 1.25GB to free up contiguous space.
  3) Drain gpu-node-17 and move pods to other nodes while we investigate compaction.
Jordan: can we do an in-place slab compaction instead of restart? runtime supports `SLAB_COMPACT=1` but it's heavier. Might be safer to restart after toggling prefetch.
Alex: do 1 + 2 now, drain node. Maria/Alex to coordinate. Jordan to monitor customer impact.
InfraBot: action: toggling PREFETCH_ENABLED on inference-prod-7 -> applying patch.
SRE-Bot: Action logged: change_set 44a2 by Alex (oncall). Rolling restart of inference-prod-7 starting.
Alex: restarting runtime...
InfraBot: runtime restart complete. New metrics: free=3.9GB, reserved=1.3GB, fragmentation_small_blocks=0.7GB.
Jordan: early signs good; no further OOMs reported in last 6m. Latency back to baseline for most tenants.
CS Lead: notifying affected customers: brief note that we saw transient errors, mitigations applied, monitoring ongoing.
DevEx: please add an entry to status page and link to incident thread. I can draft the message.
Sam: follow-up data: dmesg shows several CUDA memory mapping warnings before OOM, likely from prefetch's aggressive alloc pattern.
Maria: long-term mitigations proposed:
  - change allocator strategy to prefer smaller chunk allocations + scatter-gather to avoid large contiguous requests (engineering ticket).
  - add runtime flag to cap contiguous_alloc_size per model (configurable).
  - improve runtime compaction path to proactively defragment when fragmentation crosses threshold.
  - telemetry: emit contiguous_alloc_failures metric and alert.
Alex: also propose an operational playbook: when OOM-with-headroom happens -> 1) disable prefetch on affected runtime, 2) reduce kv_cache_reserve, 3) if repeats, drain node and escalate to infra. Add to runbook.
Jordan: assigning postmortem owners: Maria (root cause analysis), Sam (telemetry + compaction metrics), Alex (runbook update), DevEx (customer communications).
SRE-Bot: Postmortem ticket created: PM-2026-0315-alloc-stitching. Priority P2.
InfraBot: Node drain scheduled: gpu-node-17 -> cordon+evict at 2026-03-15T10:25:00Z.
CS Lead: queued customer emails, will wait 30m for stabilization before sending final update.
Alex: closing thread for live mitigation; leave open for follow-ups. Good job team. :thumbsup:
Jordan: quick note for postmortem - include a sample repro script used to trigger contiguous alloc pattern (I'll attach later).
DevEx: added status page entry draft (link: https://status.redwood.example/incidents/PM-2026-0315).
Maria: will schedule a short sync with runtime team tomorrow to discuss allocator/compaction timeline.
Sam: saving logs and heap snapshots to s3://redwood-incident-archives/3360012345/
Alex: thanks all — monitoring until node drain completes.
